title: AWS CWI Training in Beaumont, TX: 6-Day Exam Prep
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Beaumont, Port Arthur and Orange refinery, LNG and shipyard welders: corporate, online or one-to-one formats.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Beaumont: Six Days for Golden Triangle Refinery, LNG and Shipyard Welding Inspectors
html:
Between Beaumont, Port Arthur and Orange, the Golden Triangle packs in one of the country's largest clusters of refineries and petrochemical plants, newer LNG export terminals near Sabine Pass, and shipyards on the Sabine River. Pipe welders and boilermakers here grow up on turnarounds, and the step from welding to inspecting usually runs through one credential: the American Welding Society's Certified Welding Inspector (CWI). Atlantis NDT runs a six-day (6-day) exam-preparation course for that examination, aimed at Southeast Texas welders, fitters, QC technicians, NDT technicians and engineers. Choose corporate delivery at your employer's facility, online self-paced study with an instructor who answers your questions, or one-to-one sessions online or in person. AWS administers the examination and awards the certification; Atlantis gets candidates ready and certifies no one. There is no Atlantis classroom in Beaumont, and the course is not approved, accredited or endorsed by AWS. To discuss it, send a Beaumont CWI exam prep enquiry.

What the six days look like from the Golden Triangle

The course follows the structure of the exam. The first two days build Part A Fundamentals: welding processes, AWS terms and symbols, joint design, metallurgy, mechanical and nondestructive testing, discontinuities, safety and inspection math. The third day prepares for the Part B practical by measuring welds and applying procedure and qualification records. The fourth day works through your Part C code book. The fifth is timed practice papers, and the sixth revisits weak spots and covers exam logistics. A day-by-day breakdown is on the national CWI exam prep page.

The three formats deliver the same outline in different ways:

  • Corporate. A plant, turnaround contractor or shipyard brings the six days to its own facility for a group of its people. Exercises use the company's welds and gauges and, where it fits, its own code and procedures.
  • Online. A single candidate works through a study plan built on the six-day outline, with course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers, and puts questions to the instructor as they come up. No class times are set; the candidate sets the pace.
  • One-to-one. Six days of sessions with the instructor for one candidate, either online or in person at a location agreed when the booking is made.

All practice questions are original Atlantis work, written to the subject areas AWS publishes. None is lifted from the AWS examination, and Atlantis has no window into exam content or results.

Golden Triangle industries that employ welding inspectors

Refining and petrochemicals in Beaumont and Port Arthur

AWS's Beaumont page names the ExxonMobil Beaumont Refinery and Petrochemical Complex and Motiva's refinery operations as anchors of the regional economy. ExxonMobil started up an expansion at Beaumont in March 2023, adding a new crude unit and hydrotreaters after construction that began in 2019, and describes the site as one of the largest refineries in the United States. Port Arthur adds more refining and chemical capacity along the waterway. In these plants, piping is built and repaired to ASME B31.3, procedures and welder tests are qualified under ASME Section IX, and pressure equipment brings in Section VIII. Chrome-moly, stainless and alloy work makes preheat, post-weld heat treatment, positive material identification records and hardness checks part of the inspector's routine.

LNG at Sabine Pass and Port Arthur

Golden Pass LNG, a QatarEnergy and ExxonMobil joint venture at Sabine Pass south of Port Arthur, produced its first LNG in March 2026 and shipped its first cargo in April. The U.S. Energy Information Administration reports that the project aims to start its second train in the second half of 2026 and its third in the first half of 2027, after construction was disrupted in 2024 when the lead contractor filed for bankruptcy. Nearby, Sempra Infrastructure and Bechtel are building the Port Arthur LNG export terminal, and the project has already asked federal regulators to open the pre-filing process for a further expansion. Liquefaction plants are dense with cryogenic and process piping, impact-tested procedures and stainless welding, so EPC contractors and their subcontractors keep hiring piping QC inspectors through construction, commissioning and early operations.

Crude terminals and pipelines around Nederland

Pipelines carrying Permian and other crude converge on the large terminals around Nederland, and feed gas lines serve the LNG plants. Pipeline construction and repair welding is normally specified to API 1104, and station, dock and terminal piping brings in B31.3 or B31.4 depending on the system. Terminal tanks follow their own API standards, which are not CWI exam books.

Shipbuilding and repair on the Sabine

Orange has a long shipbuilding history, and Conrad operates a yard there on the Sabine River, just north of the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway, with enclosed construction bays and a marine railway; Conrad says the yard has built a wide variety of vessels for commercial and government markets. Hull, deck and frame welding follows the vessel's classification rules, the owner's specification and, on government work, the contracting agency's requirements. The CWI exam has no marine book, so yard candidates usually find AWS D1.1 the closest match.

Industrial construction, structures and maintenance shops

Pipe racks, structural steel, platforms and buildings inside the plants, and the fabrication shops that supply them, bring a steady load of D1.1 work. Many Golden Triangle shops do both: structural steel one week, spool fabrication the next.

Who hires CWIs in Southeast Texas, and what they want to see

  • Turnaround and maintenance contractors add QC inspectors for spring and fall turnarounds. Candidates who know Section IX, B31.3 and how to read a weld map and heat treatment chart get placed quickly.
  • EPC contractors on LNG and plant expansions build QC teams that track welder qualification against every joint, check material and filler traceability, and accept welds before NDT and hydrotest.
  • Owner inspection and QA groups at the refineries oversee contractors, review weld records and audit vendor shops.
  • Shipyards need inspectors who can work across structural welding, piping and class or customer requirements.
  • Third-party inspection firms place CWIs at fabricators and on site; see third-party inspection in Beaumont.

A great deal of Golden Triangle work is contract-based, which leaves many experienced welders with a patchy record of who they worked for and when. Start building that list long before you apply. For how the credential affects pay and career choices on this coast, read code inspector vs CWI salary on the Gulf Coast and CWI requirements and career impact.

Choosing a Part C code for Beaumont, Port Arthur and Orange work

AWS asks you to choose the open-book code when you apply. Its list covers D1.1 structural steel, API 1104 pipelines, D1.2 aluminum, D1.5 bridges, D15.1 rail cars and locomotives, D17.1 aerospace, the ASME option pairing Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, and an ISO option. For the Golden Triangle, the decision is mostly between three.

Most of your welding or inspection is inBook to considerPart C will test you on
Refinery, petrochemical or LNG piping and pressure equipmentASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3Essential and supplementary variables, impact testing, piping examination and acceptance
Pipelines, feed gas lines, terminal tie-insAPI 1104Procedure and welder qualification by destructive test, field acceptance criteria
Shipyard structure, pipe racks, platforms, structural fabricationAWS D1.1Prequalified joints, tolerances, visual acceptance and qualification

For a plant inspector here, the ASME book is the usual answer, because almost every weld on a turnaround is qualified and examined under those documents. Study the edition AWS names for the exam rather than whichever copy sits in the contractor's trailer. Further reading: the AWS D1.1 overview, the API 1104 summary and the guide to WPS, PQR and WPQ records, which shows how qualification differs between the three codes.

The AWS Sabine Section and where local welders train

Southeast Texas has its own AWS section, the Sabine Section, part of District 18. Its recent calendar has included section meetings hosted at a welding supply house in Beaumont and a member appreciation and awards night that doubled as officer elections. Showing up matters for a CWI candidate: meetings put you in a room with QC managers and senior inspectors, some of whom can verify your welding history for the AWS application, and they are a good place to hear which contractors are staffing for the next turnaround or LNG milestone. Details are on the section's pages at sections.aws.org.

Lamar Institute of Technology in Beaumont offers a welding Associate of Applied Science and a shielded metal arc (structural) welding certificate, and Lamar State College Port Arthur lists a welding for shipbuilding course among its workforce offerings. Many local inspectors also came up through boilermaker and pipefitter apprenticeships. These are part of the area's welding pipeline; none of them is an Atlantis partner or venue.

Booking the CWI exam from Beaumont

When AWS accepts your application, its confirmation letter includes an eligibility code. You give that code to Prometric to schedule the computer-based parts: Part A, 150 Fundamentals questions, and Part C, roughly 50 to 65 questions worked with your code book open. Prometric's site lists the test centers nearest the Golden Triangle.

The practical is a separate booking. AWS runs Part B itself at its seminar and exam locations, mixing hands-on tasks using AWS-supplied tools and specimens with 46 questions. AWS has a CWI location page for Beaumont that says its classes serve Port Arthur, Orange, Nederland, Vidor and Port Neches; when we checked in November 2026 it said the 2027 schedule would be available soon. Watch the AWS seminar and exam schedule, and be ready to travel to Houston or another city if no Beaumont session suits. AWS requires a minimum of 72% on each part and lists its exam fees on aws.org. For a full budget including travel and time away from work, see the CWI exam budget planner.

Planning study around turnarounds and storm season

Golden Triangle work follows a calendar most outsiders never see. Spring and fall turnarounds mean weeks of long shifts, LNG milestones pull crews onto overtime, and hurricane season from June through November can shut plants and reshuffle schedules with little notice. Plenty of local hands also travel to Lake Charles and the Louisiana plants between jobs. The online format suits that pattern because nothing runs at a fixed time and questions can go to the instructor from a hotel room or a break trailer. Cover Fundamentals during the quieter weeks, keep the code book with your gear, and save the timed practice papers for the run-up to your Prometric date rather than the middle of a turnaround.

For Part B, the trap for experienced pipe welders is judging by eye. Use test coupons and cut-outs to practise with fillet, bridge cam, undercut and hi-lo gauges, write each reading down, then compare it with a written limit. Between shifts, the Practical NDT welding workshop simulator lets you walk through inspection steps on a laptop.

Corporate delivery for a Golden Triangle plant, contractor or yard

A company preparing several people can have the six days delivered on its own site. A turnaround contractor can build every exercise on Section IX and B31.3, using its own weld maps and procedure qualification records. A shipyard in Orange might run the code day in D1.1 for structural inspectors and the ASME book for piping staff. A pipeline or terminal contractor can work in API 1104 using its own welder qualification files.

The practical day uses the employer's gauges on its own welds, from welder test plates to production cut-outs, so measurement practice matches the joints those inspectors will sign for. Timing is agreed around turnarounds and project milestones. Each candidate still applies to AWS individually and must meet the experience and vision rules personally; an employer cannot apply on their behalf.

One-to-one sessions for Southeast Texas candidates

One-to-one gives a single candidate six days with the instructor, either online or in person at a location agreed when booking; Atlantis has no premises in Beaumont. Online suits people on rotating shifts or working away in Louisiana. The format fits a candidate who failed one part and needs focused work on it, or a boilermaker with a firm exam date who wants a set structure. To see which parts tend to cost candidates marks, read CWI results by exam part.

Eligibility and the vision record

AWS ties its experience requirement to education. A high school diploma or equivalent calls for five years of welding-related work; an associate degree in an engineering technology, engineering or physical science field calls for two; a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology calls for one. Whether a particular Lamar credential qualifies for a shorter route is decided by AWS. The AWS Visual Acuity Record needs near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, with or without glasses, and a color perception test, done by a qualified practitioner within the period AWS allows before your exam. If your years fall short, the Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI) lets you inspect under a CWI while you build them. The full table is on the AWS CWI exam prep course page.

After the CWI: Golden Triangle career paths

AWS keeps a CWI valid for nine years, with renewal filings at years three and six and recertification at year nine. In Southeast Texas the next step usually depends on the plant you work in:

  • NDT methods. Many plant inspectors add ultrasonic or magnetic particle testing so they can run the checks themselves. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies NDT staff after training and logged method hours, and Atlantis provides that training; see NDT training in Beaumont, NDT training in Port Arthur and ultrasonic testing in refining.
  • In-service inspection. Some plant inspectors move on to API 510 or 570 certification, which API runs under its own rules; Atlantis does not train for those certifications.
  • Senior roles. The Senior CWI (SCWI) and AWS endorsements suit inspectors running QC programs; see the Senior CWI pathway.
  • Visual technique. VT Level 2 training sharpens the core skill of the CWI; see also visual testing and weld inspection.

Comparing credentials? Read AWS CWI vs API 577 vs ASNT Level II. Local pages: ultrasonic testing in Beaumont, weld inspection services in Beaumont and the Practical NDT simulator for Beaumont.

Neighbouring CWI pages and requesting a Beaumont quote

Other Gulf Coast pages: Houston, Lake Charles, Baton Rouge, Corpus Christi and New Orleans.

For a quote, tell us the format (corporate, online or one-to-one), how many candidates, each person's schooling and welding history in outline, and the Part C book each plans to choose. For corporate delivery, add the site, the gauges and sample welds available, and the turnaround or milestone dates to work around. Use the Beaumont CWI enquiry form. Atlantis quotes the course on request, and AWS publishes its own examination fees.

faq.q: Is the Atlantis CWI course held in a Beaumont classroom?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Beaumont. Individuals study online with an instructor answering questions, single candidates can book one-to-one sessions online or in person at an agreed location, and employers can host the six days on site. See the outline.

faq.q: Who awards the CWI, AWS or Atlantis?
faq.a: AWS. It sets eligibility, runs Parts A, B and C, and awards the certification to candidates who pass. Atlantis prepares candidates and the course carries no AWS approval or endorsement.

faq.q: Which Part C code suits a refinery or LNG inspector in the Golden Triangle?
faq.a: Usually the ASME option, Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, because plant and liquefaction piping is qualified and examined under those documents.

faq.q: Which code should a shipyard welder in Orange choose?
faq.a: The CWI exam has no marine book, so AWS D1.1 is usually the closest match for hull, deck and frame steel. Yard staff who mainly inspect piping may prefer the ASME option.

faq.q: Can I take the CWI exam in Beaumont?
faq.a: Parts A and C are taken at a Prometric center, booked with the eligibility code from your AWS letter. Part B is run by AWS at its seminar locations; AWS has a Beaumont page, which in November 2026 said its 2027 schedule would be available soon, so check the schedule and plan for possible travel.

faq.q: Should I do one-to-one online or in person?
faq.a: Online suits rotating shifts and work away in Louisiana; in person takes place at a location agreed when you book. The content and the six days are identical either way.

faq.q: Can a turnaround contractor run the course for its crew before the spring season?
faq.a: Yes. Corporate delivery brings the six days to your site, uses your gauges, weld maps and qualification records, and is timed around your turnaround calendar. Request a quote.

faq.q: Do the practice questions come from the AWS exam?
faq.a: No. Atlantis writes all of its practice questions and timed papers to the topic areas AWS publishes, and it has no access to the AWS examination.
The AWS Sabine Section, part of District 18. It holds meetings in Beaumont and posts its calendar on sections.aws.org.

faq.q: Does Atlantis offer NDT training in Beaumont and Port Arthur?
faq.a: Yes. Training in VT, MT, PT and UT follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and certification afterwards is your employer's job under its own written practice. See NDT training in Beaumont.
